papers.title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models have greatly improved input understanding in universal multimodal embedding models. However, this understanding does not ensure that their embeddings preserve the evidence needed to distinguish relevant items from confusable alternatives. To preserve essential discriminative evidence in embeddings, this paper proposes DiLE, a discrimination-aware latent-space learning framework that combines task guidance with on-policy retrieval feedback. Specifically, a few learnable queries are used to encode task-relevant information in a compact latent space. Reasoning instructions and auxiliary answer-generation supervision shape these representations to support both task understanding and retrieval discrimination. To address task-specific discriminative needs, we design shared-private expert adaptation that integrates cross-task knowledge sharing with task-specific representation learning. Building on this, the on-policy hard-negative distillation is introduced: the student retrieves confusable candidates, and a reverse KL divergence objective aligns its embedding-based similarity distribution with the teacher's fine-grained relevance distribution over these candidates. Candidates are periodically refreshed using updated student snapshots, tying teacher supervision to the student's evolving retrieval behavior and confusions. Across four model configurations that span two backbone generations, DiLE achieves state-of-the-art performance on MMEB-v2, UVRB, and MRMR, demonstrating its effectiveness across modalities and tasks.

summary.en: DiLE encodes task information into a compact latent space via learnable queries, combining shared-private expert adaptation and on-policy hard-negative distillation to preserve discriminative evidence, achieving SOTA on MMEB-v2, UVRB, and MRMR.
summary.zh: DiLE 通过少量可学习 query 在紧凑隐空间编码任务信息，结合共享-私有专家适配与 on-policy 难负例蒸馏，使多模态嵌入保留区分性证据，在 MMEB-v2、UVRB、MRMR 上取得 SOTA。

papers.title: Single-Transformer Latent Diffusion
papers.abstract: Latent generative models typically rely on three separate networks: an encoder that tokenizes pixels, a generator that models the latent distribution, and a decoder that maps latents back to pixels. UNITE recently merged the first two into a single generative encoder trained in one stage, but its decoder remains a separate network. We ask whether this last network can be folded in too, so that one diffusion transformer encodes, generates, and decodes. Simply letting the shared backbone decode does not help. What makes it work is to cast all three modes as position-aligned sequence maps over one fully shared backbone, distinguished only by a mode token and the timestep. The resulting model, UNIFIED, is simple: one network trained from scratch in a single stage with only reconstruction and flow-matching losses, without adversarial losses or pretrained encoders (e.g., DINO). On ImageNet-1K 256x256 at matched parameters, UNIFIED improves gFID over UNITE at three sizes (~60M, ~115M, and ~215M) and reaches 2.08 with 215M parameters, the lowest among compared models under 250M parameters. On text-to-image generation, UNIFIED-B (218M) reaches a GenEval score of 0.87 at 512x512, exceeding single-stage pixel diffusion models with around one billion parameters. Full unification of latent diffusion is thus not merely feasible but beneficial.

summary.en: UNIFIED folds encoding, generation and decoding into one shared diffusion transformer trained from scratch with only reconstruction and flow-matching losses, reaching 2.08 gFID on ImageNet-1K 256x256 and 0.87 GenEval.
summary.zh: UNIFIED 将编码、生成、解码三个模式统一到单个共享骨干的扩散 Transformer 中，仅用重建与流匹配损失从零训练；在 ImageNet-1K 256×256 上，约 215M 参数时 gFID 达 2.08，优于 UNITE，且 UNIFIED-B 在文本到图像 GenEval 上取得 0.87。

papers.title: UUBench: Understanding the Unspoken toward Full-Duplex Multimodal Interaction
papers.abstract: Effective real-time, full-duplex multimodal interaction requires systems to understand not only what users say, but also the communicative needs conveyed through prosody, facial expressions, gestures, and context, and to generate audiovisual responses that appropriately address those needs. Existing evaluations offer limited insight into whether systems translate an understanding of such unspoken needs into effective responses. We introduce UUBench, a benchmark for assessing how well multimodal interactive systems Understand the Unspoken intent and address users' implicit communicative needs. The inherent subjectivity of implicit intent inference poses a key challenge for evaluation. To address this, we introduce Process-Oriented Scoring, which grounds the assessment of intent fulfillment in observable auditory and visual cues, such as prosody and gestures. Rather than relying solely on a single overall score, it evaluates how well a response addresses the communicative needs conveyed by each applicable primitive dimension. We aggregate the dimension-level scores according to each dimension's relevance to the annotated evidence. Beyond intent fulfillment, Outcome-Oriented Scoring evaluates the naturalness, appropriateness, and human-likeness of the reply itself under audio-only, visual-only, and audiovisual conditions. To make these judgments traceable to observable evidence, we propose a Fact-Grounded Scoring JEV module, which uses structured, timestamped audiovisual observations of the user and the digital human's reply to assess one dimension or criterion at a time. UUBench provides a foundation for assessing whether multimodal interactive systems respond effectively to meaning beyond literal wording, supporting progress toward context-aware, real-time, full-duplex interaction.
papers.comment: 49 pages, 37 figures, 9 tables, including appendices. Preview version; work in progress

papers.title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds
papers.abstract: AI-driven game development holds the potential to transform diverse human inspirations into interactive experiences. However, existing systems and benchmarks primarily focus on explicit development specifications, with limited support for adapting multimodal references and evaluating actual gameplay experiences. We introduce GameAnything, an open-source agentic platform that transforms multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games through iterative development. GameAnything integrates coding agents with an independent playtesting critic, persistent development state, and reusable experience memory to support continuous refinement. We further present GameAnything-Bench, a benchmark spanning diverse reference modalities, game creation objectives, and gaming environments, with exploratory gameplay testing to assess both functional correctness and gameplay quality. Evaluations of nine coding agent configurations reveal that current agents can adapt reference content but still struggle with playable interactions and precise modifications. Moreover, multimodal references improve content fidelity, while iterative refinement yields substantial but varying improvements across agents. These findings highlight both the potential and remaining challenges of inspiration-driven game development.

summary.en: GameAnything is an open-source agentic platform that turns multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games via iterative development with coding agents, a playtesting critic, and experience memory; GameAnything-Bench evaluates nine coding agent configurations, which adapt references but still struggle with playable interactions and precise edits.
summary.zh: GameAnything 是一个开源的智能体平台，将多模态灵感通过迭代开发转化为现有游戏的可玩扩展，结合编码智能体、独立的试玩评审、持久开发状态与可复用经验记忆；配套 GameAnything-Bench 评测 9 种编码智能体配置，发现它们能适配参考内容，但在可玩交互与精确修改上仍显不足。

papers.title: Frontier models need only one text to unmask its human or AI author
papers.abstract: Given a single text and a simple zero-shot prompt (no web access, tools, candidate lists, or writing samples), frontier models can answer "who wrote this?" at three increasingly specific levels: (1) whether an AI or human wrote it, (2) if an AI, which lab, and (3) if a human, often exactly who. The latest models (Claude Fable 5.2, GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Carbon) match trained detectors like Pangram while also explaining their predictions in natural language, and Opus 5.5 names the correct lab for 98% of texts generated by models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. Most strikingly, Fable 5.2 correctly names the author of 55% of 15K anonymous ICML 2020 reviews that were never made public, and identifies the username behind 69% of comments from active Redditors (with >500 posts over the last year). Accuracy depends on exposure to an author's writing in pretraining data and on reasoning effort, and simply asking a model how familiar it is with someone predicts whether it can identify their writing. For anyone who has published enough writing online, frontier models present a greater threat to anonymity than commonly assumed, and defenses are limited.

papers.title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space
papers.abstract: Vision Banana showed that a closed image generator, instruction-tuned to paint perception outputs as RGB images, becomes a generalist vision model. Does this carry over to \emph{open} generators, and if not, what fails? We answer with \textbf{Open Vision Banana (OVB)}, an open framework that adapts the 7B diffusion generator of Qwen-Image-2.1 into one instruction-driven model for metric depth, semantic, instance, and referring segmentation, using a single shared low-rank adapter and public data. Each task is a \emph{task contract} whose RGB encoder, instruction, and decoder share one specification and are checked before training. Studying 42 externally evaluated checkpoints from two 100k-update runs, six exact weight-space merges, and eight controlled shorter runs, we find that the gap to the closed system is specific and measurable. Geometry is learned early while absolute scale is not: median-aligned NYUv2 $δ_1$ stays at 0.89--0.93 throughout training as unaligned $δ_1$ wanders between 0.11 and 0.50. The scale is not committed by a single sample: a ten-seed ensemble lifts unaligned $δ_1$ from 0.348 to 0.516 without retraining. Depth and 2D segmentation compete for the shared adapter, and weight merging moves along this trade-off without escaping it. Finally, lower validation flow loss comes with lower Cityscapes accuracy (Spearman $ρ\approx-0.9$ between loss reduction and mIoU), so the loss cannot select checkpoints. We release code, contracts, training data, and all evaluation outputs.

summary.en: Open Vision Banana adapts Qwen-Image-2.1's 7B diffusion generator with one shared low-rank adapter into a unified depth and segmentation model; across 42 checkpoints, absolute scale stays unlearned (NYUv2 unaligned δ1 0.11–0.50, 0.516 with ten-seed ensemble) and validation flow loss anti-correlates with Cityscapes mIoU (Spearman ρ≈-0.9).
summary.zh: Open Vision Banana 将 Qwen-Image-2.1 的 7B 扩散生成器通过单一共享低秩适配器调成统一模型，覆盖深度、语义/实例/指代分割；在 42 个 checkpoint 上发现尺度未被学到（NYUv2 无对齐 δ1 仅 0.11–0.50，十种子集成提到 0.516），深度与分割争用适配器，验证 flow loss 与 Cityscapes mIoU 的 Spearman ρ≈-0.9，无法用于选型。

papers.title: Polytropos: What Do Vision-Language Model Descriptions Make of a Cultural Object?
papers.abstract: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks. We introduce Polytropos, a benchmark that measures what model descriptions of cultural objects keep of the particular object by turning each description back into an image and comparing it with the original photograph. On 374 objects from the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Getty, with 1,870 descriptions from five models and 230 written by curators, reconstructions are recognised as the recorded culture more often than the photographs, at 54.55% to 59.09% against 52.14%, yet 16% to 21% of objects change outcome and only 0.49% of reconstructions are identified as the specific object. On the same objects, models lose recorded cultures at a rate similar to curators but gain more. Model descriptions give each object many faces, each typical of its culture and almost none the object itself.

summary.en: Polytropos reconstructs VLM descriptions of 374 cultural objects into images and compares them with originals: reconstructions are read as the recorded culture 54.55%-59.09% of the time versus 52.14% for photos, yet only 0.49% match the specific object.
summary.zh: Polytropos 基准将 VLM 对文物的描述重建为图像并与原照片比对，覆盖 374 件文物、5 个模型共 1,870 条描述及 230 条策展人描述；重建图被认作所记录文化的比例为 54.55%–59.09%，高于照片的 52.14%，但仅 0.49% 能对应到具体物件。

papers.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
papers.abstract: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Inspired by this, we propose ToolSmith, an automatic tool-generation framework that grows and reuses modules on top of a lean base tool library. We evaluate ToolSmith on three in-domain multimodal search benchmarks and ten out-of-domain benchmarks under a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol. ToolSmith consistently improves over the base library across deployed agents of varying scales, with larger backbones reaping greater gains, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Our code and data are available at https://threesr.github.io/toolsmith/.

papers.title: UniVEP: Unifying Velocity and Endpoint Prediction for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Flow-matching robot policies usually use one prediction target throughout action generation, even though recovering actions from noise and polishing nearly clean actions bring different challenges. We systematically compare velocity prediction (V), endpoint prediction (X), and velocity-weighted endpoint prediction (X--V) across multiple robot policies, benchmarks, and inference budgets. On StarVLA and LiLa-WAM, X--V works best for few-step generation, while V gains more from iterative refinement. We further uncover their complementary strengths across noise levels: clean actions have concentrated covariance spectra, endpoint predictions stay more stable under high noise, and velocity predictions offer more accurate corrections near clean actions. Inspired by these findings, we introduce UniVEP, which learns both prediction targets together with consistency supervision and switches from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement as noise drops. Each step only needs one network run, and joint training also boosts single-step endpoint generation. Tests on simulated and real-world manipulation show better success rates and efficiency. On RoboTwin, UniVEP hits 61.36% success with one StarVLA run, beating the best single-target baseline at sixteen runs (59.96%). With LiLa-WAM, two runs outperform the best sixteen-step single-target baseline and cut inference latency by 77.1%.

papers.title: Interpreting Diffusion Model Activations in Natural Language
papers.abstract: Interpreting the intermediate activations of diffusion models (DMs) is key to understanding how they generate images. Existing interpretability methods for DMs provide limited support for open-ended interrogation, making it difficult to extract human-interpretable insights. We extend LatentQA, the task of answering natural-language questions about Large Language Model activations, to DM activations. We introduce the Diffusion-specific Activation Oracle (DAO), which translates DM activations into natural-language answers to open-ended questions about the ongoing generation. Our experiments show that DAO can effectively describe the content of the final image from activations at early denoising steps. Additionally, we demonstrate that DAO captures the structure of the DM's activation space well enough to steer image generation toward target attributes. Furthermore, we show that attribution patching through DAO identifies DM components that contribute to visual attributes specified in natural language. Our code is available at https://github.com/yamanoko/dao/tree/main.

summary.en: Extending LatentQA to diffusion activations, DAO translates denoising activations into natural-language answers, describing final image content from early steps and steering generation toward target attributes.
summary.zh: 将 LatentQA 任务扩展到扩散模型激活，提出 DAO 把去噪激活翻译成自然语言回答，可从早期去噪步激活描述最终图像内容，并能引导生成目标属性、用 attribution patching 定位相关组件。

papers.title: ABI: Actor-Free Behavior-Induced Representations for Zero-Shot Test-Time Guidance
papers.abstract: Behavior-cloning policies show strong ability in sequential control by generating coherent multi-step action chunks, yet their purely imitative objective limits zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks. While offline reinforcement learning offers principled policy improvement, existing methods either require task-specific reward supervision or remain tied to a specific actor during critic training or policy deployment, inflating training cost and restricting cross-policy generalization. We observe that evaluating actions under the data-collecting behavior largely preserves their relative value ordering across target policies, offering a way around actor coupling. Combining this property with reward-free successor prediction, we propose Actor-Free Behavior-Induced Representations (ABI) to learn multi-horizon action-chunk representations from unlabeled trajectories without reward supervision or actor training. At test time, pairing the frozen representation with lightweight task readouts forms a chunk critic that guides target policies without parameter updates and transfers directly across distinct unseen policies. Our analysis establishes when the value ordering is preserved across policies and when selecting among proposed chunks improves closed-loop return. Across 65 locomotion, navigation, and manipulation tasks, ABI's chunk critic guides weak imitation policies to match or surpass zero-shot RL baselines with high sample efficiency, outperforms existing zero-shot critics on identical proposals, and improves externally trained RL actors without retraining. From raw pixels, ABI delivers substantial guidance gains and surpasses prior zero-shot RL baselines on visual manipulation, highlighting its potential for visuomotor control.

summary.en: ABI to learn multi-horizon action-chunk representations without rewards, guiding target policies at test time to surpass zero-shot RL baselines across 65 tasks.
summary.zh: Actor-Free Behavior-Induced Representations（ABI）方法，通过无奖励的后继预测学习多视界动作块表示，在测试时引导目标策略提升零样本泛化能力，在65个运动、导航和操作任务中超越了现有的零样本RL基线。

papers.title: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models
papers.abstract: Depth-recurrent (Looped) models raise effective depth by applying a shared stack of blocks several times. Scaling them usually requires pipeline parallelism, but commonly used interleaved 1F1B is drawn for an acyclic stage graph in which each micro-batch enters each stage once. Once that stack is split across stages, the same stage is visited several times on one micro-batch and later stages feed earlier ones: native 1F1B has no slot for the extra visit, cannot rank a first iteration against a second, and its neighbour-only send/receive order has no back edge to the first stage, so the arrangement stalls or fires out of order. We present Loop-PP, which rebuilds both the timetable and the communication for this cyclic layout. It schedules different iterations of the same stage separately, specializes a 1F1B skeleton into a globally consistent order over those visits, and emits a static instruction stream per rank that separates posting from waiting so communication overlaps local compute. Loop-PP is bit-identical to a single-stage reference. On 8B-60B MoE models, it lowers peak memory by as much as 32.8\%, and with compute budget fixed, the best observed throughput rises by 12.7\%.

papers.title: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory
papers.abstract: Exploring a scene from as little as a single photo requires generating a long, camera-controlled walkthrough that extends far beyond what was captured, yet remains consistent upon return. Memory-based video generation methods preserve what they have already seen, but have no anchor beyond it, where the camera drifts from its path and a text prompt can name objects but not place them. Layout-conditioned methods provide such an anchor and precise control over what appears where, but rely on layouts that are typically authored by hand. Both limitations arise because, beyond what was captured, nothing anchors the video model unless a human authors one. To overcome both, we propose Lyris, a long video generation framework that never leaves the video model without an anchor: a persistent point-cloud memory where the scene has been observed or generated, and a 3D layout that a vision-language model authors where it has not. Our key insight is that the interface between the two models can be surprisingly coarse. A layout of one labeled 3D box per object is simple enough for a vision-language model to author (and for a user to edit), yet expressive enough for a video model to follow once rendered along the camera path. We demonstrate walkthroughs of over three minutes and 50 meters from a single photo, passing through doorways into rooms it never shows. When evaluated on minute-long round trips across four datasets, Lyris outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a wide margin, reducing camera error by 3.8x and improving consistency upon return by 22% on average.

papers.title: Scalable Beckmann Maps Improve One-step Generation
papers.abstract: Beckmann Transport Models (BTM) learn one-step generative maps end-to-end from data, without a teacher, a distillation stage, or pretrained features. We introduce Scalable Beckmann Maps (SBM), which bring to BTM the two ingredients behind the quality of modern multistep generators: classifier-free guidance (CFG) and a training recipe that scales, while keeping sampling at a single network evaluation. CFG combines conditional and unconditional velocity or score predictions, which a Beckmann map does not have. Our guidance rests on one observation: the BTM current is a positive multiple of an autonomous denoising field, to which CFG applies as it does to a velocity. With exact denoisers this gives guided BTM. In practice we substitute the map's own conditional and null predictions for the denoisers, which requires no additional network and introduces a bias that we characterize. We show that the guided update is consistent with a guided conservation equation, and that guidance can move the boundaries between basins, sending more noise to the modes a condition favors. Trained from scratch in the latent of a representation autoencoder, SBM reaches a one-step FID of 1.6 on ImageNet 256x256 without a teacher or a feature loss, outperforming the Improved-MeanFlow baseline with 3.2x fewer FLOPs. In text-to-image generation it reaches a GenEval score of 0.86 with one network evaluation. As a world model, where we train without guidance, the recipe alone outperforms DriftWorld on all five metrics of two robot-manipulation benchmarks, with 1.9-2.8x less training compute and no pretrained auxiliary feature encoder.
papers.comment: 40 pages, 15 figures, 12 tables. Code and checkpoints: https://tullebulle.github.io/projects/sbm/

summary.en: Scalable Beckmann Maps (SBM) adds classifier-free guidance and a scalable training recipe to Beckmann transport models for one-step sampling, reaching 1.6 one-step FID on ImageNet 256x256 with 3.2x fewer FLOPs than Improved-MeanFlow and 0.86 GenEval, and beating DriftWorld on robot-manipulation benchmarks.
summary.zh: Scalable Beckmann Maps (SBM) 将无分类器引导（CFG）与可扩展训练配方引入 Beckmann 传输模型，同时保持单次网络前向采样；在 ImageNet 256x256 上以无教师和特征损失方式从零训练，达到一步 FID 1.6，FLOPs 比 Improved-MeanFlow 基线少 3.2 倍，文本到图像 GenEval 得分 0.86，作为世界模型在两个机器人操作基准的五项指标上均优于 DriftWorld，训练算力减少 1.9–2.8 倍。

papers.title: EmoRouter: Adaptive Modality Cascading for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) involves detecting the underlying emotion behind each utterance within a conversation, which is essential for emotionally aware human-computer interaction. While omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) demonstrate strong capability for MER by jointly processing modalities including text, audio, and vision, different modality combinations yield different prediction outcomes across utterances: acoustic and visual inputs can help recover annotated labels missed by text-only inference, but can also turn correct predictions into errors. Processing all modalities for every utterance is also computationally expensive. To this end, we introduce EmoRouter, a training-free, model-agnostic framework for adaptive modality cascading that selects an exit tier for each utterance along a predefined modality order. The routing is guided by prediction-uncertainty estimates derived from Conformal Prediction. EmoRouter routes each utterance through a sequence of increasing-cost modality levels and exits at the first level when the model is confident in the emotion. To determine when to exit, we propose Conformal Set Contraction, a structural calibration criterion that calibrates the per-tier CP error budgets used for these exit decisions. Comprehensive evaluations on 4 MER benchmarks and 3 Omni-LLMs reveal that EmoRouter matches or outperforms the full modalities while reducing inference latency by 67.9--94.5%. Furthermore, EmoRouter demonstrates high transferability across different models, validating its robustness. Code is available at https://github.com/tianyi-lab/EmoRouter.
papers.comment: Accepted to Transactions on Machine Learning Research, 2026

summary.en: EmoRouter, a training-free, model-agnostic adaptive modality cascading framework, uses Conformal Prediction uncertainty to pick per-utterance exit tiers with Conformal Set Contraction calibration, matching full-modality accuracy on 4 MER benchmarks and 3 Omni-LLMs while cutting latency 67.9–94.5%.
summary.zh: EmoRouter 是一个免训练、与模型无关的自适应模态级联框架，依据 Conformal Prediction 估计的不确定性为每句话选择退出层级，并用 Conformal Set Contraction 校准各层级误差预算；在 4 个 MER 基准、3 个 Omni-LLM 上，它匹配或超过全模态效果，同时将推理延迟降低 67.9–94.5%。

papers.title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering visual information that is no longer observable, such as the original location of an object. Existing approaches typically rely on full observation histories, which become redundant over long horizons, or text summaries, which may omit precise visual details. We study visual moment memory, the ability to retain such details from key moments for subsequent manipulation. To support this study, we introduce VMBench, a suite of long-horizon manipulation tasks requiring memory of spatial locations, visual appearances, and their associations. We further propose MomentMem, a hierarchical architecture in which a VLM-based memorizer selects keyframes and an executor predicts actions conditioned on the selected memories. This separation enables us to evaluate memory selection alongside closed-loop task success and to study memorizer generalization independently of the executor. On VMBench, MomentMem achieves 49.9% average success, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 31.7 percentage points. Moreover, we find that the memorizer transfers well to unseen appearances zero-shot. It can also adapt to an unseen task with only a few memory annotations, reaching 43.7% success, close to the 44.3% obtained with full memory supervision. Further experiments show competitive performance on RMBench and improvements in real-robot manipulation. These results highlight the value of retaining sparse visual evidence for memory-dependent manipulation. Our code is available at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/MomentMem.

papers.title: SAVIOR: Sample-efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for OCR Representation
papers.abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) pipelines and vision-language models exhibit high accuracy on standard OCR and document-understanding benchmarks, yet they systematically underperform on document patterns that are operationally critical in financial workflows. These patterns include vertical or rotated text, logo-embedded vendor names, fine-print regulatory clauses, degraded scans, and complex multi-column layouts. While underrepresented in public datasets, they constitute a substantial portion of real-world failure cases. We introduce SAVIOR, a sample-efficient data curation methodology that targets such high-impact failure scenarios to adapt vision-language models for robust financial OCR. We further propose PaIRS, a structure-aware evaluation metric that measures layout fidelity by comparing pairwise spatial relationships between tokens. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct with SAVIOR-Train achieves a word recall of 0.93. When the resulting layout-aware OCR output is used as context for document question answering, it attains an F1 score of 0.89, outperforming both open- and closed-source models such as GPT-4o, Mistral-OCR, PaddleOCR-VL, and DeepSeek-OCR.

summary.en: SAVIOR curates sample-efficient data for high-impact financial-OCR failures and fine-tunes Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct, reaching 0.93 word recall and 0.89 document-QA F1, beating GPT-4o, Mistral-OCR, PaddleOCR-VL and DeepSeek-OCR; PaIRS measures layout fidelity.
summary.zh: SAVIOR 针对金融 OCR 中的旋转文本、logo 内嵌名称、细小条款与退化扫描等高频失败模式做样本高效数据筛选，并用 Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct 微调；配套的 PaIRS 指标衡量布局保真度，词召回达 0.93，文档问答 F1 为 0.89，超过 GPT-4o、Mistral-OCR、PaddleOCR-VL 和 DeepSeek-OCR。

papers.title: Feedback Shortcut: Speculative Decoding for Latent Feedback Transformers
papers.abstract: Feeding each position's top-layer hidden state back into the next position's input improves Transformer performance. However, this feedback breaks speculative decoding, since verifying a drafted token requires the top-layer state from its preceding position, which forces the draft to rely on an approximate stand-in. Training the model to adapt to this stand-in can lower the exact-decoding performance ceiling, while using it at inference time further introduces approximation error. We propose Feedback Shortcut to address both bottlenecks. First, state alignment trains a lightweight projection from multi-token prediction head states to stand-ins, leaving base model training untouched. Second, pipelined correction re-evaluates each draft using its predecessor's newly computed state, a much closer proxy to true feedback. Running this correction inside the verification pass of subsequent drafts improves accuracy with zero extra calls. Across 135M and 780M scales, Feedback Shortcut stays within $10^{-4}$ bits per byte of the exact-decoding ceiling on Paloma and accelerates decoding by 2.4-2.8x with about 2% more training compute than the latent feedback Transformer. At large batch sizes, skipping correction still preserves Transformer speed and over 80% of latent feedback's gains.

summary.en: Feedback Shortcut combines state alignment, which projects multi-token prediction head states into feedback stand-ins, with pipelined correction that re-evaluates drafts during verification, staying within 10^-4 bits per byte of exact decoding on Paloma while speeding decoding 2.4-2.8x with ~2% extra training compute.
summary.zh: Feedback Shortcut 用 state alignment 训练轻量投影，把多 token 预测头状态映射为反馈替代量，再用 pipelined correction 在验证阶段重评草稿，在 135M 和 780M 模型上将 Paloma 上的 bpb 差距控制在 10^-4 内，并实现 2.4–2.8 倍解码加速，仅增约 2% 训练算力。

papers.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
papers.abstract: Robot policies must adapt to the speed of moving objects, yet existing benchmarks rarely measure this ability across diverse tasks and speeds. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). Objects are transported through physical contact with a visibly moving belt. Each task has a static counterpart, and each evaluation episode uses the same randomized scene at all 13 speeds. We fine-tune eight vision-language-action and world-action models on demonstrations spanning the full speed range, comparing observations from the current frame alone with those including two past frames. For six models, the success rate peaks at intermediate speeds, and their failures indicate that they tend to produce actions suited to the average demonstration speed rather than to the actual one. Past frames raise the success rate by 10-40 percentage points for three models, and linear probes show that the belt speed is also most linearly decodable from these three. Adding ground-truth speed input to four of the models improves all of them, and a speed estimated from the images keeps most of this gain. These results show that SWEEP-Bench exposes speed-dependent failures and suggest that past frames help only policies from which the speed is most decodable, such as those pretrained on multiple frames. Project page: https://damin3927.github.io/SWEEP-Bench

summary.en: SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks, evaluates embodied policies across varying speeds, revealing that models often fail by outputting actions suited to average demonstration speeds rather than actual ones.
summary.zh: SWEEP-Bench是一个包含80个传送带操作任务的仿真基准，用于评估具身策略在不同物体运动速度下的表现。通过对8个vision-language-action和world-action模型的测试发现，大多数模型的成功率在中等速度时达到峰值，且倾向于产生适应平均示范速度而不是实际速度的动作，而引入过去帧或速度输入可以显著提升性能。

papers.title: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training
papers.abstract: Reasoning domains have shaped the post-training recipes of frontier models even though they are trained and deployed in domains beyond math and code. In this paper, we study the consequences of directly adopting reasoning-centric training recipes, e.g., the use of outcome-based rewards for reinforcement learning (RL), injection of "cognitive" behaviors such as proposing and backtracking from hypotheses in reasoning chains, etc., for knowledge tasks. We hypothesize that these decisions, while useful for reasoning, inadvertently encourage models to memorize hallucinations they themselves generate in their long reasoning chains when trained on knowledge tasks. To study this, we train models with standard post-training, extract their self-generated hallucinations during RL, and track memorization throughout the rest of training. Our experiments on six open models across two model families and two architectures confirm our hypothesis. We find that models' recall of hallucinations reinforced during training increases by 4.83% on average, compared to just 0.17% for self-hallucinations that receive no training signal. In fact, models even memorize false facts that they immediately retract in their reasoning; a backtracking template inherited from reasoning-centric training that has no benefit for knowledge recall. Furthermore, we find that memorization is strongest on the hardest training questions, and rewarding a hallucination makes the model less likely to abstain from it later (by 7.23% on average). Overall, our work identifies and systematically studies a previously unexamined pathway through which models learn hallucinations during training.

papers.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
papers.abstract: AI agents accumulate conversations, images, and documents through long-term interactions with users. Answering later questions often requires connecting evidence across these records, yet the resulting understanding is rarely retained, allowing mistakes to recur on related questions. Existing multimodal memory methods largely focus on storing and retrieving records, with limited mechanisms for learning from completed tasks and consolidating task-specific experience. We therefore propose MMMem, a task-aware multimodal memory framework that extracts and consolidates experience from completed tasks through four complementary strategies. First, source-linked multi-view memory organizes original text, images, and rendered pages alongside generated scene images that combine clues across records for retrieval. Second, source-generated tasks support knowledge alignment at two levels: warm-up consolidates source knowledge into task-relevant experiences in external memory, while self-training adapts the model's parametric knowledge to task demands. Third, the same vision-language model distills completed tasks into experiences that record the task context, conclusion, and support links. Finally, task-aware retrieval recalls source views and relevant experiences for answering and verification, while source-supported reuse guides long-term retention. Across three memory benchmarks and two vision-language readers, MMMem outperforms eight baselines. With Qwen3.5-9B, MMMem achieves relative gains of 36.9%, 17.6%, and 15.2% over the best-performing baselines on LoCoMo, Mem-Gallery, and LooGLE v2, respectively. Ablations show consistent gains from training and memory warm-up, while case studies illustrate how individual components work in practice.

papers.title: From Rewarding What Models Say to How They Think: Attention Process Reward Model for LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an important component in large language models (LLMs). However, existing RL approaches focus on final outputs or textual solution trajectories, leading to coarse-grained rewards and unreliable reasoning. Such paradigms focus mainly on what the model outputs while overlooking how the model internally reasons. Therefore, can we reward how a model thinks internally rather than merely what it says? We first reveal the problem of textual reward aliasing in existing reward modeling approaches. Motivated by this, we propose the Attention Process Reward Model (APRM), which assigns internal rewards based on hidden states and attention maps to capture high-quality reasoning patterns. With only approximately 46M parameters, APRM is trained using ranking and counterfactual objectives, and its reward guides RL optimization while being periodically updated to handle distribution shifts. Integrated with representative RL methods, APRM achieved an average pass@8 gain of 2.88\%. Our results demonstrate the promise of incorporating internal reasoning signals into RL for LLMs.

papers.title: GHC:Expanding Residual Interfaces in Hyper-Connections
papers.abstract: Hyper-Connections expand residual capacity across parallel streams, yet restrict every branch to narrow read and write interfaces: each branch still reads a single stream mixture and writes scaled copies of one output vector to all streams. To lift this bottleneck, we propose Grouped Hyper-Connections (GHC). By partitioning each branch into parallel groups along attention heads or FFN channels, GHC supplies each group with a distinct stream mixture and aggregates their separate outputs into each stream with learned weights. Extensive experiments across dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models show that GHC consistently improves upon Identity Hyper-Connections (IHC) with negligible parameter and memory-access overhead, increasing training efficiency by 35% over Pre-Norm and 10% over IHC. Moreover, expanding residual interfaces overcomes the diminishing returns of adding streams, allowing wider residual states to yield further gains.

papers.title: PixelOne: From Options to Pixels in a Single Forward for GUI Grounding
papers.abstract: GUI grounding requires precise clicks at low latency. Recent models such as GUI-Decisions and GUI-Swift predict coordinates in one forward pass using fixed global bins with local refinement. However, screenshot downsampling removes detail needed to locate small controls, while fixed bins cover larger pixel ranges at higher resolutions. We introduce PixelOne, which transfers spatial knowledge from a search teacher to a student that predicts clicks directly from screenshots at native resolution. The teacher uses VideoJEV's text-option scorer to select rows and columns and progressively zoom into candidate regions. The student inherits the teacher's parameters and matches its distributions over explored regions through spatial distillation alongside box supervision. At inference, the same decision head selects a visual token, and a lightweight pixel head predicts the click within it, all in one forward pass. A click-aligned loss encourages pixels inside the target box to score above those outside. Across four benchmarks, PixelOne-Pro-35B-A3B achieves 83.8% mean accuracy, the highest among the evaluated single-forward grounders, with a mean latency of 0.43 s per target.

papers.title: SuperNav-1.5: Structured Spatial Memory For Agentic Navigation Systems
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of scene-level memory design for efficient navigation across sessions and successive object goals. Recent methods commonly represent a scene using scene graphs or image--text records. However, dense scene-graph representations impose substantial reasoning and context overhead on multimodal large language models, while image--text records cannot be directly converted into executable geometric routes. To address these limitations, we propose SuperNav-1.5, an agentic navigation system equipped with a structured spatial memory constructed by the agent. The memory consists of an area-segmented occupancy map annotated with agent-maintained, map-grounded memory nodes. This map guides the agent toward unvisited areas and provides executable routes to known locations. For multi-session navigation, we introduce agent-guided relocalization, whereby the agent infers an area prior from current observations and stored memory records to constrain geometric matching and localize the robot within the stored map. Together, these designs enable efficient navigation across session and successive object goals. Experiments show that our method outperforms baselines on single-object, multi-object, and demand-driven navigation benchmarks, with particularly strong gains in path efficiency. Multi-session evaluation demonstrates that the constructed memory can be reused, while deployment on a real quadruped robot further shows the system's applicability. Project Page: https://zju3dv.github.io/SuperNav-1.5/

summary.en: SuperNav-1.5 introduces a structured spatial memory system with area-segmented occupancy maps and memory nodes for efficient multi-session and multi-goal navigation, outperforming baselines in path efficiency and real-world robot deployment.
summary.zh: SuperNav-1.5 采用一种由区域分割占用图和记忆节点构成的结构化空间记忆系统，结合智能体引导的重定位技术，实现了高效的跨会话及多目标导航。实验表明其在单目标、多目标及需求驱动导航基准上超越基线，显著提升了路径效率，并成功部署于真实四足机器人。

papers.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in the physical world constitutes a Radio-Frequency (RF) radiance field, providing rich information for 6G communication and sensing. However, existing neural RF field methods suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they predominantly rely on per-scene optimization and cannot generalize to unseen scenes; (2) they require costly reference RF measurements in each target scene; and (3) they degrade severely when extrapolating beyond the vicinity of reference measurements. To overcome these limitations, we present RadioWorld, a general framework that adapts a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, without requiring any reference RF measurements at inference. Specifically, RadioWorld couples two specialized modules within a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture: a Scene-Understanding Transformer that encodes 3D scene geometry and transceiver locations to extract environment-aware global EM propagation features, and a Field-Generation Transformer that attends to these features to synthesize the RF radiance field with the local query conditions. We also establish UrbanRF-Bench, a large-scale ray-traced benchmark spanning 657 urban scenes and 32,850 RF radiance fields across seven global cities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RadioWorld significantly outperforms specialized baselines and accurately synthesizes RF fields at arbitrary locations in unseen cities. Code, datasets, and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

summary.en: RadioWorld transfers a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields via a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers, encoding 3D geometry and transceiver locations without reference measurements; it also introduces UrbanRF-Bench (657 scenes, 32,850 fields) and clearly outperforms specialized baselines in unseen cities.
summary.zh: RadioWorld 用双流 Mixture-of-Transformers 架构把世界模型迁移到射频辐射场合成，Scene-Understanding Transformer 编码 3D 场景几何与收发机位置，Field-Generation Transformer 据此生成射频场，无需参考测量；并构建覆盖 657 个城市场景、32,850 个射频场的 UrbanRF-Bench，在未见城市上显著优于专用基线。
